name: Beninu
overview: Beninu is a male Levite mentioned in the book of Nehemiah. He is identified specifically as a Levite in Nehemiah 10:9 and is named on the sealed covenant document recorded in Nehemiah 10:1-27, specifically in verse 13. His mention highlights his role within the Levitical community during the post-exilic period.
namesAndTitles: The name Beninu means 'our son' and is a proper name as recorded in Nehemiah 10:13. This name does not appear to be given directly by God but reflects a common Hebrew naming practice.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture explicitly records that Beninu is a descendant of Levi, affirming his Levitical heritage as noted in Nehemiah 10:13. Beyond this tribal connection, no additional family relationships are documented.
scriptureSignificance: Beninu's significance lies in his inclusion among the Levites who sealed the covenant in Nehemiah 10, demonstrating his participation in the communal commitment to uphold God's law after the return from exile. His presence on the sealed document underscores the important role of the Levites in leading and maintaining covenant faithfulness in Israel during this critical restoration period.
